drills.q: Your app depends_on db and connects immediately at startup. It works locally every time but fails intermittently in CI. Diagnose.
drills.a: depends_on without condition: service_healthy only waits for the container to start, not for the app inside to be ready. CI machines are often slower/more loaded, widening the window between container start and actual readiness (e.g. Postgres data dir init/WAL replay). Fix: add a healthcheck plus condition: service_healthy.

drills.q: A service's healthcheck flaps healthy/unhealthy only during its first 15 seconds after cold start, then is rock solid. What's the fix and why not adjust retries/interval instead?
drills.a: Increase start_period to comfortably exceed the measured cold-start time. Adjusting retries/interval would also affect steady-state flap detection and could mask a genuine post-startup problem that appears later.

drills.q: How would you actually force a genuine port replacement (not addition) across override files if the Compose Specification supports it?
drills.a: Use the Compose Specification's merge directives (!reset/!override in newer spec versions) to explicitly replace rather than merge that key; absent that, avoid duplicating the value across files -- only set it in whichever file should own it.

drills.q: A teammate commits their docker-compose.override.yml with local debug ports exposed to everyone. What's the actual process fix, not just telling them not to commit it?
drills.a: Add docker-compose.override.yml to .gitignore from project start, and provide a checked-in docker-compose.override.yml.example template for developers to copy locally -- the mechanism meant to stay local can't leak by accident.

drills.q: A service with profiles: [debug] is also depended on unconditionally by an always-on service. What happens when you run plain docker compose up?
drills.a: Compose still starts the dependency to satisfy depends_on, effectively activating the profiled service implicitly even without its profile being requested -- profile gating isn't airtight against an unconditional depends_on.

drills.q: docker compose config shows the environment variable you expect, but the running container's printenv shows something different. What else could be overriding it?
drills.a: The image's own baked-in ENV instructions from build time, or the application's own config-loading logic (e.g. a .env file loaded by an app library inside the container) further overriding what Compose passed in -- docker compose config shows what Compose passes in, not necessarily what the process ultimately uses.

drills.q: How would you prove, after the fact from logs, that a sleep-based race actually caused a failure rather than some other cause?
drills.a: Correlate the app's connection-failure timestamp against the dependency container's own 'ready to accept connections' log line timestamp. If the app's first attempt is earlier than the dependency's actual ready line, that's direct proof of the race.

drills.q: A service has no healthcheck defined. What does docker compose up --wait do for it?
drills.a: Nothing extra -- a service without a healthcheck is considered healthy the instant it starts since Compose has nothing to poll. --wait gives zero additional readiness guarantee; the actual fix is adding a real healthcheck.

drills.q: A one-shot migration container exits with code 0 but the migration actually failed silently. What does Compose's condition: service_completed_successfully do, and how do you prevent this class of bug?
drills.a: Compose considers the dependency satisfied since it only checks exit code 0 -- it has no visibility into internal logic failures. Prevention is at the app level: ensure migration scripts propagate real failures as non-zero exit codes instead of swallowing exceptions.

drills.q: Compare Compose's restart policies and explain why the default (no) is wrong for a long-running local dev service.
drills.a: no/always/on-failure[:N]/unless-stopped. The default (no) means a service that crashes once just silently stays down, which is a worse local-dev debugging experience than a service that restarts and re-surfaces the same error on a loop, useful as recurring signal -- though restart: always during active debugging of a crash loop floods logs and should be temporarily disabled.
